clauses.statement: The squared bilinear norm of any finite monomial expansion is exactly its Hankel coefficient quadratic form.
Positive-measure Hankel matrices are positive semidefinite; positive definiteness is equivalent to the support threshold and positivity of all leading Hankel determinants, including order zero.
The canonical monic polynomial is the normalized bordered Hankel determinant, and its next coefficient is the explicitly indexed shifted Hankel determinant ratio.
Finite Hankel determinants are products of the monic norms, and norm and recurrence coefficients obey the norm, beta, and shifted alpha determinant ratios whenever their denominators are nonzero.
For the actual spectral measure the Hankel matrix is the Krylov Gram matrix and it is positive definite exactly up to the Krylov grade.
Canonical polynomial coefficients and recurrence data are smooth on each finite positive Hankel coordinate system; no representing measure in a neighborhood is assumed.
Differentiating the actual moment pairing gives the product rule, and differentiated monic orthogonality gives the lower-degree polynomial variation and squared-norm variation.

The actual alpha and positive-order monic beta derivatives are the moment variation evaluated on their explicit monic sensitivity polynomials, with the equivalent adjacent-polynomial alpha form and a separate total-mass derivative at order zero.
For every fixed polynomial coordinate chart the actual Euclidean Jacobian, in alpha-then-mass-and-beta output order, is the displayed coefficient sensitivity matrix.
The absolute condition number is the spectral norm of the actual Jacobian; the normwise relative condition number includes the input/output norm factor.
